2609.03734.title: Beyond BLEU: A Case for Redefining Sign Language Translation Benchmarks
2609.03734.paper_summary: BLEU-4 is the standard metric for evaluating sign language translation (SLT), but spoken-language metrics may not adequately reflect sign language proficiency. The multimodal, low-resource context of SLT allows models to exploit spurious correlations and spoken-language priors, rather than learning stronger sign representations. In this paper, we evaluate the relationship between spatio-temporal understanding and BLEU-4 across six SLT models on Phoenix-2014T and CSL-Daily, showing that gains in BLEU-4 are not on their own evidence of better sign language understanding. This work introduces an alternative inspired by language-learning assessment, using an open-weight-LLM QA protocol that measures salient content preservation. It aligns more closely with human rankings and is six to seven times more paraphrase-invariant than BLEU-4. Applied to SLT, this protocol targets content transfer, is more robust to train-test overlap, and gives a different picture of the field: the five gloss-free systems are largely within noise of one another on Phoenix-2014T, while the gloss-supervised system stands 9.3 points higher, a gap invisible to BLEU-4.
2609.03734.paper_summary_zh: BLEU-4 是評估手語翻譯 (SLT) 的標準指標，但口語語言指標可能無法充分反映手語能力。SLT 的多模態、低資源環境使模型能夠利用虛假的相關性和口語語言的先驗知識，而不是學習更強的手語表徵。在本文中，我們評估了在 Phoenix-2014T 和 CSL-Daily 上六個 SLT 模型之間的時空理解與 BLEU-4 之間的關係，顯示 BLEU-4 的提升本身並不證明手語理解的改善。這項工作引入了一種受語言學習評估啟發的替代方案，使用開放權重的 LLM 問答協議來測量顯著內容的保留。它與人類排名更為接近，且在意譯不變性方面比 BLEU-4 高六到七倍。應用於 SLT，這一協議針對內容轉移，更加穩健於訓練-測試重疊，並提供了該領域的不同視角：在 Phoenix-2014T 上，五個無手語標記的系統彼此之間的差異幾乎在噪音範圍內，而手語標記監督系統則高出 9.3 分，這一差距在 BLEU-4 中是不可見的。
